sections.overview: Lethrinus borbonicus, the snubnose emperor, is a reef-associated marine fish in the family Lethrinidae.
sections.identification: It has a blunt snout, molar-like side teeth and a dark grey or yellow-brown body; it reaches about 40 centimetres total length.
sections.habitat: It ranges through the western Indian Ocean, from the Red Sea and Persian Gulf to Réunion, and shelters over sand near reefs by day.
sections.diet: At night it forages over reef flats and slopes, eating echinoderms, molluscs and crustaceans.
sections.behavior: It may gather in small groups by day but is solitary at night.
sections.reproduction: FishBase lists maturity at about 21 centimetres, while detailed spawning information is limited.
sections.ecology: It is a congener of the Atlantic emperor, Lethrinus atlanticus, but lives in the western Indian Ocean; its blunt snout and molar teeth contrast with that species’ pointed snout and conical teeth.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment dated 2018 classified it as Least Concern.
